title: The World Cup Starts on Wednesday. For NRIs, It Is in Their Backyard for the First Time.
excerpt: Forty-eight teams, 104 matches, 16 venues across the US, Canada, and Mexico. Here is everything the Indian diaspora needs to know about watching and attending the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
body:
The FIFA World Cup starts on Wednesday. Not in Qatar, not in Russia. In Mexico City. Then Los Angeles. Then Toronto. Then every major city across North America for the next five weeks.

For the estimated 4.4 million Indian Americans and the broader South Asian diaspora living across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, this is the first World Cup they can attend without crossing an ocean. India is not playing. That has not stopped the excitement.

## The Numbers Are Staggering

https://x.com/FIFAWorldCup/status/2064097133163102294

The 2026 World Cup is the first to feature 48 teams, up from 32. That means 104 matches across 16 venues in three countries, from the opening fixture in Mexico City's Estadio Azteca on June 11 to the final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. Twelve of the 16 venues are in the United States. Two are in Mexico. Two are in Canada.

For NRIs on the East Coast, MetLife Stadium in New Jersey will host the final. For those on the West Coast, the LA Stadium in Inglewood — the same venue that hosted the 2028 Olympics — will host the USA's opening match against Paraguay on June 12. For the Bay Area diaspora, Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara hosts Qatar vs Switzerland on June 13. For those in the Pacific Northwest, BC Place in Vancouver has Australia vs Turkey on the same day.

## The Broadcast Confusion Is Over

After months of uncertainty — during which both Zee Entertainment and a Washington DC-based firm called AVNI LLC claimed to hold the India broadcast rights — the situation has largely resolved. The FIFA World Cup will be broadcast in India on Zee's newly launched Unite8Sports channels, with live streaming on Zee's digital platforms. In the US, Fox Sports and FS1 will carry all 104 matches, with Spanish-language coverage on Telemundo and streaming on Peacock.

For NRIs who want to watch in the US, the simplest path is Fox and FS1. In the UK, the BBC and ITV have the rights. In Canada, coverage will be on TSN and CTV.

## The Opening Week

The tournament kicks off on Thursday, June 11 (Wednesday night in India) when hosts Mexico face South Africa at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. The match starts at 3 PM Eastern, which is 12:30 AM IST — a familiar late-night timeslot for Indian sports fans who grew up watching Premier League football.

The marquee first-week fixtures for the diaspora:

- **June 11**: Mexico vs South Africa, Mexico City (3 PM ET / 12:30 AM IST)
- **June 12**: USA vs Paraguay, Los Angeles (9 PM ET / 6:30 AM IST)
- **June 12**: Canada vs Bosnia and Herzegovina, Toronto (3 PM ET / 12:30 AM IST)
- **June 13**: Brazil vs Morocco, New York/New Jersey (6 PM ET / 3:30 AM IST)
- **June 13**: Qatar vs Switzerland, San Francisco Bay Area (3 PM ET / 12:30 AM IST)
- **June 14**: Netherlands vs Japan, Dallas (4 PM ET / 1:30 AM IST)
- **June 14**: Germany vs Curaçao, Houston (1 PM ET / 10:30 PM IST)

## No India, but Plenty of Indian Roots

India did not qualify. But the World Cup will not be entirely devoid of Indian connections. As The Videshi reported earlier this week, four players of Indian origin will take the field across different national teams — a quiet but significant milestone for the diaspora's relationship with the world's most popular sport.

The broader context matters too. Football's footprint in India has grown substantially since the 2022 World Cup. The Indian Super League now draws consistent television audiences, and the national team's recent performances under Igor Štimac's successor have raised expectations for the 2030 cycle. The 2026 World Cup, happening live in NRI time zones and NRI cities, could accelerate that trajectory.

## What NRIs Should Know

If you are attending a match in person, know that FIFA has implemented a digital-only ticketing system through the FIFA+ app. Resale is restricted to the official FIFA platform. Stadiums in the US will enforce strict bag policies similar to NFL games — clear bags only, no larger than 12" x 6" x 12".

For those watching from home, the time zones are friendly. Almost all group-stage matches fall between 12 PM and 10 PM Eastern Time, which means 9:30 PM to 7:30 AM IST. Weekend matches, in particular, will land in prime viewing hours for NRIs in North America.

The final at MetLife Stadium is scheduled for July 19 at 3 PM Eastern — 12:30 AM IST on July 20. Set your alarms now.
